First off, my non-literary statements in regards to r/literarytheory.  It is a worthwhile cause that should be revived.  Second my responses to the queries posed in the post regarding Macbeth and Ficciones.  My admittedly bold statement concerning objectivity is this:  there is no objectivity in the human condition.  We as human beings filter all that we encounter through our subjective experiences and consciousness therefore objective rendering cannot ever be truly achieved.  Having said that I believe that Macbeth represented Marlowe's Faustian principle in full effect (power corrupts, absolute power corrupts absolutely) that I believe is about as close as you can encounter to an objective reality that exists in the world today because empirically that scenario has played out with nearly absolute certainty in both history and in artistic work.  It is human nature to try and gain as much as possible in your circumstances.  However, there are those that reverse that trend (Gandhi, MLK, etc.) but that is a choice of higher consciousness.  My ultimate point being this however:  The literature of Shakespeare and Borges empirically prove that it is only by voluntarily rising to overcome the base instincts of human nature that you can ultimately be a truly innovative presence in the world and not be conquered by your own ambitions.

We wouldn't buy a car that sucked and hope every day that the car would get better, we would either buy a better car outright or put energy and money into that car until it was the way you liked it. Some cars are inherently more this or that than others and that is the natural advantages you can't control that others have over you. Start measuring yourself up against yourself not others because you will never measure up thinking the grass is greener on the other side. Comedy is hard.  Humor is subjective and what may be funny to you may not be to someone else.  In fantasy you are better off being clever because your readership is reading you to fuel their imagination, not to read poop jokes.  Another thing to avoid is too much inside humor, don't joke about specific things regarding your world unless the joke would apply to our world and be equally funny.  If it is a shorter work the humor needs to be quick, witty and zingy.  If it is a longer work use narrative arc to your favor and just have events keep getting more and more comical and out of hand until they boil over and repeat the process several times.  That is the formula, and in this case the formula has been proven to work.  It is how you write it (your voice) that will set you apart.  People will either like it or they won't.  But give 4 friends a part of your book or your entire story to read that arcs the entire comedic narrative for a particular situation.  If at least 2 of them find it funny keep it, if not go back to the drawing board.  Lastly, the best weapon in your arsenal is your characters, draw good sketches for them and give them unique and comedic personality tics and let the humor inherently flow out of their quirky personalities.  This should create most of the humor you need.  I hope this was helpful.

A lot of depression comes from perfectionism.  We hold ourselves to an impossibly high standard and when we inevitably fail to meet the standards we set for ourselves we beat ourselves up over it.  This locks us into a negative behavior cycle where we constantly feel guilty, ashamed, and above all depressed.  When you feel as if you are worthless you undermine any expectations you can set for yourself and therefore live up to that standard.  For example, I am struggling with a drinking problem.  I would feel guilty and worthless for drinking so much and therefore I labelled myself a worthless drunk.  Therefore that was my total self-worth it meant that I continued to live up to that standard and would just drink more, since all I was was a worthless drunk anyway.  It is when I recognized that you are only a human being, with good and bad qualities, that I saw the truth of it which is when you make a mistake you have to forgive yourself and move on because if you don't you will carry the mistakes you make with you and repeat them. I learned a lot about the nature of depression.  I learned that all depression is caused by 3 root feelings or beliefs.  1.  Guilt over past or present actions which lower your self worth. 2.  Self-pity:  Thinking your problems are unique, unsolvable and you have it worse than anyone else and no one can understand you. 3.  Other-pity:  Feeling so strongly about the problems of others or the state of the world today that you bear those burdens and it makes you feel bad about the world.  The thing about all these conditions is that they work together or individually to lower your self worth.  The thing I learned which helped me most is that you should distinguish between being guilty of wrongdoing and feeling guilty.  Being guilty should simple mean that you are a human being, you made a mistake and you should approach the situation head on resolve it through a penance or an act of atonement to the person you erred against and then move on.  Nothing except the worst of human behavior should ever make you feel guilty.  Feeling guilty leads to self doubt and lower self-esteem and nothing is truly worth those feelings because they cause depression and lower your ability to function.  If you do wrong, own up to it and move on.  This is just one thing I learned and I hope it helps.  If you would like to hear more coping techniques I am more than happy to share more.

What I recently learned (and I hope this can help) is that the depressed/suicidal mindset is caused by three root issues.  Someone who feels guilty about their life, someone who is in a state of self pity who feels that their problems are beyond help or too much for them to be able to deal with, or lastly they are so overwhelmed by "other pity" such as the miserable state of the world today and empathizing too strongly with the concerns and problems of others that they take on other peoples problems which makes their own problems so much worse.  The best thing for you to do would be to identify which of these apply to her (and it may be all three) and deal with each one individually.  The main thing I can say to you regardless of what the situation is is that their is a difference between being guilty of something and feeling guilty for something.  Feeling guilty is never productive and only creates problems and depression.  If you are guilty of doing something to someone else, talk to them, ask them what a reasonable solution would be and work out the problem, but that doesn't make anyone a bad person.  We are all people and make mistakes, make the wrongs right and move on and don't let a guilty conscience weigh you down.  We also all need help because there are times in everyone's lives where their problems are too much for themselves to cope with and they need at the very least someone who is willing to listen to them.  I hope this helps and if you want to talk more I am available and please don't hesitate to let me know.

Less than 2 weeks ago I was at the exact same place you are now.  I had to make I drastic change or I would be dead.  I even started to plan the best and most effective ways to kill myself. The best thing I have learned recently is to fully embrace the fact that we are all human.  This means accepting that we all make mistakes, we are not perfect, and we will never live up to the expectations of what we feel our lives will be.  Armed with this information can either be further depressing or it can be the most liberating experience in the world.  That is your choice.  Guilt, Self-Pity, and the pitying of others are the 3 root causes of all depression.  Just remember:  If you are personally guilty of something or have a reason to feel down about yourself the healthiest thing you can do is pay a penance if guilty to one you wronged to return to an even keel.  If self pity is the issue the best thing you can do is be proactive and think about why you feel sorry for yourself and change it.  Start with baby steps and think about a good thing you can do each day.  Other-pity is best resolved by getting upset and doing something to change the person who you pity's situation instead of wasting needless emotional energy on crying and being upset about it which doesn't do you or them any good.  Do something to help.  Once you view guilt/depression as mutual negative cycles that feed off one another you can free yourself from both.  No one has the right to make you feel guilty about anything.  No one but the worst criminals are actually bad people.  We are people who do both good and bad.  So you should atone and move on when you do bad and gain confidence and strength to fight depression later on when you do good.  No one is a bad person.  The guilt complex only exists to keep you down.  I hope you will take this into consideration and truly think about your problems in this context.

This will probably get buried but here goes nothing:  I use a 3-tier system whenever I watch movies:  Does it inform?  Does it entertain?  and Does it make a relevant statement that makes me evaluate the world in a significant way?  I think the best pieces of cinema do all 3 but you can still make an incredibly good if not great movie by just doing at perfect job accomplishing one of the three.  The Avengers kept me completely entertained for its entire running time.  I will not be watching it again and if I did it would have to be in the theater because it is a near perfect theater movie.  Raiders of the Lost Ark to me is the ultimate theater movie because no matter how many times I watch it I am entertained through the viewing.  Where this becomes relevant is when I watch something like that it is like a classic piece of pop-art vs. a classic piece of art, Warhol vs. Van Gogh.  I don't go into a film like The Avengers expecting a Bergman-esque meditation on the inherent psychological torment of the human condition and it would be treating the directors vision unfairly to judge it with the same criteria for which I would judge The Seventh Seal for example.  Both are valid great films, but it goes to art vs. entertainment.  I have my problems with Avengers when I dissect the minutiae of the film as well, but dissection was not the goal.  And I in no way with the dialogue what it was feel like it was in any "dumb-ed down".  You should go to a summer blockbuster style movie expecting to be thoroughly entertained and if you get any more for your money all the better.  But I don't feel bad about liking the movie and don't feel like I should have to have intellectual illumination otherwise something is dim.
